items.text: Adults 21 and over may possess, use and carry up to 2.5 ounces (about 71 g) of cannabis, of which no more than 10 g may be concentrate (28-B M.R.S. 1501). Use is allowed only in a private home (including its yard) or on private property not open to the public where the owner permits it. It is banned while driving or riding as a passenger in a vehicle on a public way, and smoking it is banned wherever tobacco smoking is banned. Breaking these rules is a civil offence with a fine of up to US$100 (about A$142 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026).

laws.rule: Maine drivers may not use, manipulate or talk into a hand-held phone or electronic device while driving on a public way, including while stopped in traffic, at a light or at a stop sign (29-A M.R.S. 2121). Drivers 18 and over may use hands-free mode, or a single swipe, tap or push on a mounted device in view of the road. A device may be used to call emergency services, or once the vehicle is pulled off the road and can safely stay stopped.
laws.penalty_signal: Traffic infraction: up to US$50 for a first offence and up to US$250 for later ones (about A$71 and A$355 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026)

laws.rule: Texting while driving is a separate offence, including when stopped in traffic or at a light or stop sign (29-A M.R.S. 2119).
laws.penalty_signal: At least US$250 for a first offence (about A$355); at least US$500 (about A$710) and a licence suspension of 30 days or more for a repeat within 3 years
